The only per-kWh cost figure it gives is the U.S. Department of Energy cell cost target of $80/kWh[2], and it says that current manufacturing costs are current manufacturing costs are about double this figure[3]. For the NFA cathode, Table 1[4] gives an estimated energy density improvement of 250–275[5] Wh/kg, which is an energy figure, not a cost. The NFA pouch cell results in Fig. 7[6] are reported only as formation and cycling data.
